about.title: Fairfield Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Fairfield never expect a hospital visit to leave them worse off than when they arrived. Yet in a city of roughly 113,000 in Solano County, some patients do walk out with a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error that a careful provider should have caught. Some of those visits begin as emergencies after a collision on I-80 or Air Base Parkway; others are routine appointments that went wrong. Either way, California's MICRA rules shape what happens next. You generally have one year from the day you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to file. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before suit. And because a poor result by itself is not malpractice, a qualified medical expert almost always has to explain where the standard of care was broken. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Fairfield patients with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: MICRA's Clock Is Shorter Than People Assume
items.desc: California generally allows one year from discovery of the harm and never more than three years from the injury, plus a 90-day notice before filing. Getting connected early keeps those windows open.

items.title: Cases Need a Medical Expert, Not Just a Story
items.desc: A bad outcome alone is not malpractice under California law; a qualified expert usually has to show where the standard of care was breached. The attorneys in our network know how to build that piece.

items.title: The Damages Cap Changes Every Year
items.desc: MICRA limits non-economic damages, but that cap rises annually. An independent attorney can explain which figure applies to your timeline and how economic losses are handled separately.

items.question: An emergency room near Fairfield missed my fracture after a crash on I-80. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but the question is whether a reasonably careful ER provider, seeing the same X-rays and symptoms, would have caught it. That usually takes review by a qualified medical expert, not just a second doctor's opinion. Your crash claim against the other driver and a potential malpractice claim are separate matters with different deadlines, so it helps to discuss both with an attorney early.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice case in Solano County?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and in most situations no more than three years from the date the harm occurred. You also have to give the provider 90 days' written notice before a lawsuit is filed. Because those periods can overlap in confusing ways, it is worth having an attorney calculate your specific dates.
